answer: Retirement resets standing, so a rotated key inherits nothing and must rebuild stake from zero. Each agent bonds a stake into the canyon registry, and peers may slash only the identity that signed the disputed claim. A forger needs one fresh bond per identity, so a thousand fakes cost a thousand stakes, not one. Honest clusters accrue continuous standing through a shared lagoon ledger, while farms show hollow histories of freshly bonded keys. Rotation buys no head start, so attack cost scales with identities created and the defence prices fakes out.
